extracted.intended_audience: engineers, students, and technical readers interested in dynamo design and electrical engineering
extracted.subtask_description: Review and critical evaluation of an engineering textbook (The Construction of Dynamos) with attention to its usefulness to designers and students, accuracy of technical content, and adherence to standard practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contains new practical matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Either it must contain new matter of practical importance not hitherto treated in such a way as to be useful to the designer, or it must be an improvement in the way of treating old and well-known matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new publication on a well-covered subject is justified only if it provides genuinely new practical content or presents familiar material more clearly/usefully for students and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness to designers versus students
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader should be left with the impression whether the designer of dynamos will learn anything from it, and whether the student may with equal advantage read other popular treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the book actually aids practicing designers (practical design guidance) or is primarily suitable for students/readers seeking a popular exposition; the author himself should not present illustrative examples as full design procedures if the book purports to cover design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and completeness of theoretical treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatment of theory (e.g., magnetic field, testing iron, magnetometric method, hysteresis) should be complete and not misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that methods are presented with their limitations (e.g., magnetometric method applicable only to thin and long wires and not to turned iron rods; need to eliminate solenoid effects). Point out missing proofs (e.g., area of hysteresis loop as work lost) and incorrect numerical claims (e.g., hysteresis coefficient values).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness of numerical values and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical figures and claims (for example hysteresis coefficients and the significance of eddy current losses) must be accurate and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag values that are 'much too large' or statements that contradict known practice (e.g., saying eddy-current losses are very small in dynamo work when actual losses exceed theoretical values due largely to eddy currents at burrs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of formulas and generality (multipole vs two-pole)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where formulae are given (e.g., E.M.F. formula), include the general/more useful forms (e.g., formula for a multipole machine instead of only two-pole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer inclusion of general formulas and mention when an author omits useful generalizations that practitioners will expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability of design methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Design methods should reflect actual practice (e.g., in practice speed is usually given and the dynamo must be designed to suit it, not the reverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid design procedures that start from arbitrary choices (e.g., selecting speed freely) rather than typical real-world constraints; illustrative design examples should not assume unrealistic freedoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical use of formulae and common-sense checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Design should not proceed by blind application of 'output formula' or other formulae without critical investigation and common-sense reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should verify formula-derived dimensions against practical considerations (example: formula gave 93 in × 15½ in but common-sense suggested 80 in × 20 in would be better and cheaper). Warn against relying solely on formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of standard practice (coverage and selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim that space is 'almost exclusively devoted to machines representing present standard practice' should be borne out by the content; inclusion or omission of standard vs non-standard machine types matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the book actually covers standard practice (e.g., presence/absence of common alternator types) and call out inclusion of non-standard or experimental machines as not representing present practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and scale of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should be useful and appropriately scaled; overly large scale illustrations that occupy space can restrict explanatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether figures help or hinder: large-scale illustrations may waste space and limit useful text; illustrations should aid comprehension and be proportioned to textual needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good practice in construction details
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructional details (e.g., armature housing, armature supports) should reflect good, accepted practice, not merely modern or peculiar arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out details that 'may be modern, but are certainly not good practice' and prefer proven, standard construction methods over novel but questionable details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of explanations and reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations (e.g., why field magnets are laminated) must be correct and aligned with accepted understanding rather than 'novel' but incorrect accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: saying field cores are laminated 'to prevent eddy currents due to any sweeping of the field caused by armature reaction' was judged beside the mark; correct reasoning (e.g., lamination when stator slots are wide/open) should be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of indiscriminate recommendations (context-sensitive advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations for remedies or devices (e.g., damping coils for hunting) must consider context and may be harmful in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn against blanket endorsements: damping coils recommended without caveat may be 'absolutely harmful' when applied to alternators driven by gas engines; advice should specify applicable situations and contraindications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate framing of illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of design should be clearly labelled as illustrations and not presented as full substitutes for practical design practice; the author himself notes 'examples of design are introduced by way of illustration only.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure readers understand limitations of illustrative examples; if the book purports to teach design, exemplars should be sufficiently rigorous or accompanied by caution about their illustrative nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of scope (theory, design, construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Book should deliver on its stated scope (theory, design, and construction) with proportional treatment and not promise more than it supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether chapters devoted to different aspects match the preface claims; mismatches (e.g., saying to treat design but then providing only illustrative examples) reduce usefulness.
